problem: Vision-and-language navigation and language-only human-robot interaction make instruction hard for people in indoor spaces: exact turn angles are hard to verbalize, commands must be given in the robot's frame, and the target is often occluded or ambiguous among several instances of the same object. Prior gesture-based HRI systems rely on depth or time-of-flight sensors.
motivation: Pointing is one of the most natural human communication channels and is faster than verbal description. A robot asking bystanders for directions in cluttered, narrow indoor spaces needs a monocular-camera-only way to share perspective with the human and resolve ambiguity. The 360-degree views from nearby locations differ a lot in such spaces, so one-step sharing of spatial understanding fails.
key_idea: Estimate the human's pointing direction from a monocular image (3D body pose plus head pose), navigate to an intermediate goal 1 m from the person along the pointing ray to obtain a shared visual perspective, then run language grounding on that view to pick the final target.
insight: Splitting gesture-based commanding into pointing-direction estimation (a shared perspective as intermediate goal) followed by language grounding makes the system robust to arbitrary pointing directions and to targets outside the robot's initial view. Gesture resolves ambiguity among multiple grounded instances, and grounding refines the coarse pointing. No quantitative ablation is given; the evidence is qualitative real-robot demonstrations.
method: Body-skeleton gesture estimation: monocular 3D human pose network gives a human-centric frame with the origin at the pelvis; the pose is up to a non-metric scale and is rescaled using the estimated depth.
Head-pose gaze estimation: an OpenFace-style face pose network (Biswas et al.) is fused with the body pointing direction to offset the 35-50 mm 3D pose error that grows with distance.
Geometric monocular depth: distance d = f_y*H_c/|b_y - c_y| from the bottom of the person bounding box (feet on the floor, zero camera pitch) gives the scale and the robot-to-person transform.
Intermediate goal and navigation: a pose on the prebuilt 2D occupancy map 1 m from the instructor along the pointing ray; ROS move_base with the TEB local planner drives there using odometry.

Language grounding: Google Cloud speech-to-text converts the command to text, then ZSGNet (zero-shot grounding) runs on the shared-perspective image with a 0.60 classification-score threshold. It is retrained on MIT Indoor Scenes (15K+ images) plus indoor Visual Genome region descriptions.

Final goal selection: pointing direction disambiguates multiple grounded boxes; the robot moves along the pointing direction while tracking the target until there is no navigable space or the target leaves view.

setting.backbone: Pretrained 3D human pose net + face pose net + ZSGNet (retrained on indoor data) + Google speech-to-text; classical geometry and ROS planner
setting.training_data: ZSGNet fine-tuned on MIT Indoor Scene Recognition (>15K images) merged with indoor-subsampled Visual Genome region descriptions; other modules are off-the-shelf
setting.observation: monocular RGB camera, audio (speech), wheel odometry, prebuilt 2D occupancy map
setting.action_space: continuous 2D goal poses executed by ROS move_base/TEB planner
setting.privileged: prebuilt 2D occupancy map of the environment; static-environment assumption; foot-floor contact point visible for scale

numbers_note: No quantitative results; the paper only gives qualitative real-robot demonstrations (occluded shared perspective, referring to a third person).
results: Qualitative demonstrations on a Double2 telepresence robot show the pipeline navigating to a chair in an occluded view among multiple chairs, and chaining the pipeline through a referral to a third person. The authors report no metrics and only claim qualitative advantages over depth-sensor-based gesture systems (SVP, VGPN).
limitations: No quantitative evaluation or baselines; only qualitative demos.
Scale estimation requires the person's feet/floor contact to be visible; face pose fails when the instructor is far away; grounding trained on a small custom indoor dataset.
Assumes a prebuilt static occupancy map and a cooperative human who avoids colliding with the robot.
